newsitem.title: CHINA: No China role in snagged merger - Cable & Wireless.
newsitem.headline: No China role in snagged merger - Cable & Wireless.

text.p: Cable & Wireless Plc said on Friday China had not played a role in the breakdown of the firm's planned merger with British Telecommunications Plc.
"The Chinese government was not a factor in the discussions coming to an end," said Rod Olsen, chairman of the Asia Pacific development board at London-based Cable & Wireless.
"There was a fruit salad of reasons as to why the merger could not take place," he told reporters.
The reasons included overlapping partnerships for the two telecommunications giants in Europe and the United States and an inability to obtain anticipated shareholder value, he said.

Telecommunications analysts in Hong Kong and elsewhere had said Cable & Wireless's 57 percent owned Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd unit might have been one of the reasons for the failure of the merger earlier this year.
China would have to give its assent to any merger involving the Hong Kong operations.
Hong Kong Telecom is a key asset of Cable & Wireless and there has been much market speculation over its role in Hong Kong after the British colony reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, 1997.
Hong Kong Telecom formerly was the monopoly provider of telecommunication services in Hong Kong. It lost its domestic monopoly last year but has exclusive rights on international traffic until 2006.
Cable & Wireless officials, speaking after the company announced the formal opening of a Beijing office, said they expected China to honour all existing commitments.

China has been eager to take stakes in key sectors in Hong Kong. Speculation about its possible interest in telecommunications was fanned after Beijing's China National Aviation Corp took a 36 percent stake in one of the colony's air carriers, Hong Kong Dragon Airlines.
Despite statements from Beijing that the move was purely a commercial deal, there was much speculation in Hong Kong that it was politically inspired.
China-controlled CITIC Pacific Ltd already has a minority stake in Hong Kong Telecom but CITIC is seen as a financial investor with little clout in China's telecommunications sector.
Cable & Wireless officials declined to say whether China had approached the company to buy any of its stake in Hong Kong Telecommunications.
"It is no secret it is a very attractive asset," said Cable & Wireless chief executive Richard Brown.

Asked by reporters if a change in the company's shareholding was expected, he said: "Any change will involve a commercial reason for doing so... Long-term shareholder interests will guide what we do."
